title: Rubio to Visit Mumbai and Jamnagar Oct. 17-22 for Energy, Strategic Talks
excerpt: The US Secretary of State's second India visit this year pairs strategic-partnership talks with business meetings and a stop in Reliance's refining hub, with energy cooperation at the centre.
body:
• US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will travel to Samarkand, Mumbai and Jamnagar from 17 to 22 October, the State Department announced on 13 October.
  • In India — his second official visit this year — he will meet senior officials on the strategic partnership, regional and global issues, and prospects for enhanced energy cooperation.
  • He will also meet business leaders to promote commercial investment and economic cooperation between the two countries.
  • The Jamnagar stop puts the itinerary in Gujarat's refining hub, home to Reliance Industries' refining complex, as energy sits at the centre of the agenda.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio will visit India next week for talks focused on the strategic partnership, energy cooperation and investment, the US Department of State said in a media note dated 13 October. Rubio will travel to Samarkand in Uzbekistan and then to Mumbai and Jamnagar in India from 17 to 22 October.

The Itinerary

Rubio begins in Samarkand, where he will take part in the C5+1 Ministerial with Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Kyrgyz Republic, and hold bilateral meetings with senior officials from all five countries. He will lead a US commercial delegation of more than 200 business leaders on that leg, which the State Department described as a historic visit for US-Central Asia commercial cooperation.

He then travels to India for his second official visit this year. His previous visit, from 23 to 26 May, was for the Quad Foreign Ministers' meeting in New Delhi hosted by External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, according to reporting by The Hindu BusinessLine. This time the stops are commercial and energy centres rather than the capital: Mumbai, India's financial hub, and Jamnagar in Gujarat.

Why Jamnagar Matters

The State Department did not explain the Jamnagar choice, but the city is home to Reliance Industries' refining hub, described in wire reporting as one of the largest refining complexes in the world. BusinessLine noted that Jamnagar hosts the world's largest single-site refinery, with capacity to process 1.4 million barrels of crude a day, and recalled a March announcement by President Donald Trump that Reliance would invest in a new refinery at Brownsville, Texas.

Energy has been a recurring point of friction as well as cooperation. Wire reports ahead of the visit noted that India has been among the largest buyers of Russian crude since 2022, and that the India stop falls just after an 18 October deadline cited in US legislation on duties targeting buyers of Russian energy. That timing gives the energy discussions in Mumbai and Jamnagar a sharper edge than a routine partnership review.

A Wider Resumption of Engagement

The visit follows other signs of renewed high-level contact. US Ambassador to India Sergio Gor said on Monday that Prime Minister Narendra Modi and President Trump had spoken the previous week and that further developments in bilateral ties were expected, according to The Times of India. Speaking in Kolkata at an event marking 250 years of American independence, Gor pointed to cooperation in defence, information technology and healthcare, recent joint military exercises, the presence of US F-35 aircraft in Rajasthan for the first time, cross-border investment, and India's role supplying generic pharmaceuticals to the United States.

What to Watch

No specific agreements have been announced in advance. The readouts after Rubio's meetings with senior Indian officials and business leaders will show whether the energy agenda produces concrete commitments — on crude purchases, refining investment or both — and whether the strategic-partnership language translates into new defence or technology initiatives. For Indian-American business and energy interests, the Mumbai business meetings are the part of the programme most likely to generate follow-on deals.
